wu: Warm-up: 'Find the Match' — Students receive half of KET speaking cards (e.g., 'What's your favorite hobby?') and mingle to find the matching response ('I like playing football'). They must say the full sentence to complete the match.
wuAlt: Alternative 1: 'Two Stars and a Wish' — Students write two positive things about their partner's last weekend and one wish for the next.
Alternative 2: 'Quick Quiz' — Teacher asks KET-style questions (e.g., 'Where do you live?'), students answer in pairs.
pres: Presentation: Show KET speaking part 1-2 frames on the board (e.g., 'Could you tell me about...?' / 'I think... because...'). Model a dialogue with a complication (e.g., 'I love music, but I can't play any instruments'). Check understanding by asking students to repeat the frames and add their own example.
presAlt: Alternative 1: 'Roleplay Demo' — Teacher and a student act out a KET speaking task with a disagreement, highlighting 'I agree, but...' phrases.
Alternative 2: 'Flashcard Sort' — Students sort phrases into 'Agree' / 'Disagree' columns, then use them in a simple dialogue.
prac: Guided practice: 'Complication Cards' — Students draw a card with a topic (e.g., 'school') and a complication (e.g., 'you don't like homework'). They practice using KET frames to discuss, with the teacher monitoring and prompting for agreement/disagreement language.
pracAlt: Alternative 1: 'Agreement Race' — Teams race to complete sentences with 'I agree' or 'I disagree' + a reason.
Alternative 2: 'Pair Drill' — Students take turns asking KET questions and responding with a complication, swapping roles after 2 minutes.
ls: Listening slot: Play a KET speaking part 2 audio where two students discuss a topic with a disagreement. Students listen and tick the phrases they hear (e.g., 'I see your point, but...'). Then, they compare in pairs and report back to the class.
re: Reactivation game: 'Stand Up, Sit Down' — Teacher reads a statement (e.g., 'I agree with homework'). Students stand if they agree, sit if they disagree, and must say a reason why.
prod: Production task: 'Roleplay with a Twist' — Students work in pairs. One is a KET examiner, the other a candidate. The candidate must answer questions using KET frames, but the examiner adds a complication (e.g., 'What if you had no money?'). They swap roles after 3 minutes.
rw: Reading and writing slot: Students read a short KET-style email (60 words) about a problem (e.g., 'I can't go to the party'). They write a reply (60 words) agreeing or disagreeing with the problem and suggesting a solution, using KET frames.
st: Story + goodbye: Read a short story about a student preparing for KET speaking. Close with: 'Today we practiced KET speaking with complications — well done! Thank you, class.'
g: Students match questions to responses in pairs, then swap cards with another pair.
Students stand in a circle and pass a ball, saying 'I agree' or 'I disagree' about a topic.
Teams race to write a KET dialogue with a complication on the board.
Students race to write KET speaking frames from memory on the board.
Students ask a KET question and the next student must answer with a complication.
diff: Fast finishers: Write a 3-sentence dialogue with two complications using KET frames.
Support: Use a sentence starter frame (e.g., 'I think... because...') to help with responses.
hw: Homework 1: Find a video about KET speaking on YouTube and summarize it in 3 sentences.
Homework 2: Write a KET-style email to a friend agreeing or disagreeing with their plan.
Homework 3: Practice KET speaking part 2 with a family member and note one phrase they used.
tip: Encourage students to use Moroccan cultural examples (e.g., 'I agree with celebrating Eid, but...') to make the language more personal and relevant.
